newsitem.title: USA: US spot resids mostly steady, crude, natgas slide.
newsitem.headline: US spot resids mostly steady, crude, natgas slide.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices mostly held steady Monday, but trade again was thin, and some expected softer crude and natgas prices to soon undermine resid, industry sources said.

"(Firm) crude helped the numbers (resid prices) for a while, but gas is key and it's finally taking its toll," said one cash trader, noting fuel switching has slowed utility burns and autumn typically means even softer demand.
In New York Harbor, prompt one percent again was unchanged at $17.50 a barrel, traders said.

NYH 0.3 percent low pour and high pour notionally held steady at $20.25-50 and $19.75-20.00, respectively, but most expected sluggish utility demand and increased supply next month to soon pressure HP.
At the U.S. Gulf Coast, one percent slipped 25 cents to $16.25-50 on reports a trader was agressively offering barrels.
USG three percent held at around $14.75. Traders said a USG three percent piece sold late Friday at $14.75 but details of the deal were not known.
New York city gate swing gas prices fell several cents Monday to the $2.10-20/mmBtu area versus NYH one percent resid at a $2.77/mmBtu equivalent.
